prerequisites: Having passed the course Thermal Engineering

learning_outcomes.text: Solve basic heat transfer problems (advanced): systems with heat generation and systems with thermal exchange by radiation using the effective sky temperature parameter (star thermal circuit).
Provide the basic design of extended surfaces (fin) that satisfy given working conditions.
Identify when a problem requires transient regime analysis.
Solve simple heat conduction problems by applying numerical methods.
Describe and identify the different types of heat exchangers.
Perform the analysis and basic sizing of a heat exchanger.
Describe the main modifications of the Brayton cycle: intercooling in compression, regeneration or recuperation, and reheating.
Describe the fundamental parts, components, and devices of steam power cycles.
Perform thermodynamic analysis of steam power cycles and modified Brayton cycles.
Identify the most important operating parameters of steam power cycles and modified Brayton cycles and establish the values of these parameters that optimize their operation.
Describe and analyze the incorporation of renewable energies and cogeneration schemes in steam power cycles and in simple and modified Brayton cycles.

syllabus_topics: TOPIC 1. Heat transfer in extended surfaces. Introduction. General equation. Fins of uniform cross-section. Fins of variable cross-section. Efficiency. Design considerations.
TOPIC 2. Transient heat conduction. Introduction. Systems with negligible internal resistance. Conduction in a semi-infinite solid. Multidimensional effects. Numerical methods in heat conduction.
TOPIC 3. Heat exchangers. Types of heat exchangers. Overall heat transfer coefficient. Thermal design of heat exchangers: logarithmic mean temperature difference method and efficiency-NTU method.

TOPIC 4. POWER CYCLES FOR STEAM TURBINE THERMAL POWER PLANTS. Rankine cycle with water/steam. Influence of operating parameters on cycle performance. Techniques for cycle improvement: superheating, reheating and regeneration. Cycle parameters. Thermodynamic analysis. Plant diagram and equipment. Technological aspects of steam power plants.
TOPIC 5. BRAYTON CYCLE. Irreversibilities in the Brayton cycle. Modifications of the Brayton cycle: regeneration, compression with intercooling, reheating. Exergetic analysis.
PRACTICE 4 – Simulation of power cycles for steam turbine thermal power plants.
teaching_methods: Problem-based learning (theoretical content exposed during problem solving)

assessment_methods.method: Continuous Evaluation (EvC1): Written exam on Block I content
Continuous Evaluation (EvC3): Written exam on Blocks II & III content
Unique Evaluation (EvU1): Written exam on all course content

assessment_rules: The course has two evaluation paths: Continuous Evaluation (EvC) and Unique Evaluation (EvU). For EvC, a minimum of 4.0/10 is required in each activity (EvC1, EvC2, EvC3), including individual practical activities, otherwise the overall grade is Fail. EvU requires a minimum of 4.5/10 in the main exam (EvU1) and 4.0/10 in each practical activity (EvU2). If practices are not completed during the semester, a separate practice exam with a minimum score of 5.0 is required to pass.
